title: The Arrivals
logline: Continuum no importa franquicias. Importa personas.
description: The flagship personal project developed inside Continuum. It is developed manga-first: approved story structure becomes a draft, a panel script, rough and final manga, and only then an anime adaptation.
_note: This manifest registers the project's documents in two ways. Entries under 'documents' are explicit: their lifecycle is written here. Files matching a rule under 'conventions' are registered by name the moment they are committed; their lifecycle transcribes the author's own Status line through 'status_lifecycle' (first match wins), so the committed documents stay the single source of truth. A Markdown file matched only by 'discover' appears as unfiled and is never treated as approved.
_note_standing: maturity (ROUGH, DETAILED, PRODUCTION_READY) transcribes how developed the author says a document is; authority (RULE, CORRECTION, INDEX, CONTENT) transcribes an 'authoritative' workflow rule, correction or source-of-truth index; overrides lists only the partial precedence a document states in its own text. Nothing here resolves a conflict the documents do not resolve themselves.
_note_board: 'episodes' declares the readiness levels of the production pipeline rules and the document categories each level requires (all approved). The episode board is computed from the committed documents on every read; nothing about an episode's readiness is stored here. 'resolves' shows a voice-check iteration still marked in review as resolved once the episode's GREEN LIGHT exists; its own lifecycle is left as its author recorded it.
_note_sources: 'page_counts' names each page total: the base panel scripts' own totals and the integrated provisional totals read from the approved production overlay's table (declared current). 'production_sources' lists, in order, the documents a chapter package is built from for an episode: episode documents, season overlays and project-wide bibles and addenda, each resolved from committed approved documents by category and scope. 'supersedes_header' honours a document's own Supersedes line.
